concerns.text: T005 specifies baseline_results.csv columns 'task_id, accuracy, nodes_visited, inference_time_seconds, token_count (plus status)', but contracts/baseline_results.schema.yaml requires 'latency_ms' (not inference_time_seconds), requires 'strategy', forbids additionalProperties (so token_count is invalid), and sets nodes_visited minimum 1. As written, T005's own verification (test_baseline_schema.py::test_baseline_columns) cannot pass — the task is unexecutable until the column list is reconciled with the contract.

T001 says 'Compute and log the SHA-256 of data/raw/locomo.jsonl in the run output (do not write to state/)', directly contradicting Constitution Principle III / Data Hygiene ('Every file under data/ is checksummed in the project's state/... artifact_hashes map') and plan Phase 1.1 ('store in state/'). An implementer following T001 verbatim produces a non-compliant run; the checksum-recording destination must be specified consistently.

concerns.text: T001 produces data/raw/locomo.jsonl while the plan, data model, and data flow all specify data/raw/locomo.csv. Downstream consumers reference the CSV path; the implementer cannot know which is canonical. Pick one path/format and update all references.

concerns.text: T002 writes noisy graphs to data/processed/graphs/graph_noise_42.json and T004 asserts that path, but the plan and data model specify data/processed/noisy_graphs.json. The noisy-graph artifact path is inconsistent across artifacts; T004's pre-execution assertion will fail against whichever path the other tasks don't produce.

T006's verification says 'tests/unit/test_runner_schemas.py column checks for Lazy and Greedy CSVs pass' but does not state WHICH contract family the CSVs are validated against: lazy_results.schema.yaml / greedy_results.schema.yaml use latency_ms and omit token_count, while execution_log.schema.yaml requires inference_time_seconds and token_count. The two contract families cannot both be satisfied by one output file; the task must name the target schema per output.

T002 implements edge REPLACEMENT ('same edge count as the clean graph but different targets') while the spec's Edge Cases and Assumptions sections define noise as ADDING a fraction of random edges to E. The spec contradicts itself (FR-001 says replace); the implementer cannot determine the required inject_noise semantics. Reconcile to one definition (spec root cause).
